title: The Immune System Explained I - Bacteria Infection
subject: Biology
beats: You're under attack every second; your body runs an army with guards, soldiers, intelligence, factories
Shows the full system: 12 jobs, 21 cells, a tangle of interactions
Makes it readable: color per job, central color for main duty
Admires the complexity, then zooms into a few cells for one infection
A rusty nail breaks the skin; bacteria enter and double every 20 minutes
Guard cells (macrophages) swallow up to 100 intruders each
Inflammation: guards order blood vessels to flood the battlefield; that's the swelling you feel
Neutrophils arrive, fight so hard they kill healthy cells, and self-destruct after five days
The dendritic cell, the brain, takes samples and decides: anti-virus or anti-bacteria forces
It travels a day to the lymph node where billions of T cells wait
T cells pass harsh training; each has a specific set-up; the dendritic cell seeks the match
Match found: helper T cells multiply; some become memory cells
Helpers activate B cells, weapons factories, when set-ups match
Helpers tell exhausted factories 'don't die yet', and let them die when it's over
What do B cells make? Antibodies, proteins built to grab one intruder
At the wound things get dire; guards die; helpers urge them on
Antibodies flood in, stun bacteria, tag them for macrophages; the balance shifts
Infection wiped out; most immune cells self-destruct to save resources
Memory cells remain for next time
This was a very simplified explanation, ignoring many players and the chemistry
Life is complicated, but understanding it reveals wonders

quote: Don't die yet, we still need you, keep going!
